title: A Bible object built from the text
description: One object (objects/<id>.json): its parts, every number in cubits with the verse it comes from, and whether each is stated in the text or an interpretive choice. objects/README.md explains each field.

slug.description: The page's address on the site, /<slug>.

summary.description: One sentence on what the object is.

license.description: The spec's license: CC BY 4.0, as for everything in objects/ (objects/LICENSE).

sources.description: The passages that describe the object, as OSIS references or ranges. The reader shows the object's glyph after the first verse of each.

unit.description: The unit of every length in the file.

assembly.description: "Build from the text": the order the parts appear in, each with the verse shown as its caption.

effect.description: What the step does to a part already built, instead of bringing it in: gild turns its wood to gold.

ref.description: One verse as an OSIS reference: Exod.25.10.

range.description: A verse or a run of verses in one chapter: Exod.25.10 or Exod.25.10-22.

quote.description: The words of the verse that state the fact, exactly as the repository's KJV and BSB have them. The check finds each in its verse.

fact.description: Something the text says about a part, with the verse that says it.

dim.description: A number. Stated in the text: interpretive false, with the verse and the words that give it. An interpretive choice: interpretive true, with a note saying why; a ref is optional.

values.description: The numbers this choice sets, by name.

option.description: A debated choice: every reading is listed, one is the default, and the viewer can switch between them.

interpretive.description: true when the part's form goes beyond what the text gives (it is labelled Interpretive choice); false when the text gives its form.

note.description: What the text gives and what the model adds.

dims.description: The part's numbers, by name, in cubits unless their unit says otherwise.

model.description: How the part is drawn: procedural:<generator> (geometry made in code from the dims), or a glTF file under models/ with its author and license.
